note: Attacker-controlled raw input bytes are wrapped in FuzzData for parsing.
First byte selects the on-demand action (0=get_string, 1=get_bool, etc.).
Remaining input is split on the separator; strings[0] becomes the JSON document.
The JSON document is copied into a padded buffer of length+32 bytes with zeroed padding.
Stage 1 parses the document and builds structural indexes; stage 2 on-demand iteration begins.
Iterates over top-level values; for an array document, each element is visited.
Returns a pointer into the padded buffer at the next structural index; for a truncated array the index can be len (start of padding).
The value's json pointer is set to the token position; for a truncated array this points at the zeroed padding.
When action=0, get_string calls parse_string on the token; if the token is a quote, string parsing proceeds.
Reads 32 bytes at src; for an unterminated string, src advances past the real data into the zeroed padding.
src advances by 32 bytes per iteration; with no closing quote in the padding, src moves past the padded buffer end.
If a backslash byte is encountered (from memory past the padded buffer), handle_unicode_codepoint is invoked.
Calls hex_to_u32_nocheck with a pointer 2 bytes past the backslash; the read extends beyond the allocated padded buffer.
Reads src[0] through src[3] (4 bytes) from a pointer that has advanced past the end of the padded buffer, causing an UNKNOWN READ detected by UBSan.
